subject: math
title: Organize Data: Sort, Count, Tally Charts and Graphs
seo_title: Grade 1 Organize Data Worksheets: Sorting, Tally Charts, Picture and Bar Graphs with 3 Categories
standard_text: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 data worksheets: sort and count shapes, read tally charts, picture graphs and bar graphs with up to 3 groups, and answer how many in all, how many more and how many fewer. 100 first grade practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Sort it, count it, show it.
key_sub: Sort things into groups and count each group. A tally group with a line across is 5. Each picture or grid line is 1. In all means add; how many more or fewer means subtract.
body_html:
The big idea

Data is information we collect, like votes or things we count. First we sort things into groups. Then we count each group. Then we show the numbers in a chart or graph. In Grade 1, a graph has up to 3 groups.

Sort and count

Put the same shapes together. Touch each one as you count it.

Tally chart

Make one mark for each thing. The 5th mark goes across the first 4. So a group with a line across is 5.

Picture graph

Each picture stands for 1. Count the pictures in a row.

Bar graph

Find the top of the bar. Look straight across to the number. Each line is 1 more.

Ask and answer questions

In all means put together, so add. How many more or how many fewer means compare, so subtract.

How many in all?

How many votes were there in all?

Apple 7, Banana 3, Grape 5. 7 + 3 + 5 = 15.

Answer: 15 votes

How many more?

How many more votes did Apple get than Banana?

Apple 7, Banana 3. 7 − 3 = 4.

Answer: 4 more votes

How many fewer?

How many fewer votes did Grape get than Apple?

Grape 5, Apple 7. 7 − 5 = 2.

Answer: 2 fewer votes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a tally group as 4, or as 64 marks and 1 line across is 5
Counting a shape twice or skipping oneTouch or cross out each one as you count
Reading the bar next to the one you wantPut your finger on the name first
Adding when it asks how many moreHow many more or fewer means subtract
Answering a name when it asks how manyHow many wants a number, like 4 votes
Counting the groups instead of the thingsIn all means add the numbers in each group

faq.q: What does organize data mean in 1st grade?
faq.a: It means sorting things into up to 3 groups, counting each group, and showing the counts in a tally chart, picture graph or bar graph. Then students answer questions like how many in all and how many more.

faq.q: How do you teach tally marks to first graders?
faq.a: Make one mark for each thing, and draw the 5th mark across the first 4. Then count the groups by 5s and add the extra marks, so one group and 2 marks is 7.

faq.q: How do you read a bar graph in Grade 1?
faq.a: Put your finger on the name under the bar, go to the top of the bar, and look straight across to the number. In Grade 1 each line on the graph is 1.

faq.q: How do you find how many more on a graph?
faq.a: Read the two numbers, then take the smaller one away from the bigger one. If Dog has 8 and Cat has 5, there are 8 − 5 = 3 more.

sets.title: How many in all, how many more, how many fewer

items.q: How many crows and finches came in all?
items.e: Read the bars. Crow: 2. Finch: 3. In all means add: 2 + 3 = 5 birds.
Count the pictures. Lily: 6. Zoe: 2. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 6 − 2 = 4. The answer is 4 more books.
